clue.text: Sculpture say most unsuitable I caught in area (7,3)

indicators.note: whatever is caught in a net or trap ends up held inside it, so LAST I C goes inside PART

blocks.note: a part of town is an area; it opens to hold the rest
the last person you'd pick is the most unsuitable
c = caught on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: A critic calls a sculpture the least suitable piece they have ever seen in the area.
annotation.walkthrough: 'caught' does double service: it is the cricket abbreviation C, and with 'in' it also tells you where LAST, I and C go.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'say': sculpture is one of the arts that shape material, which is what plastic art covers.

clue.text: Media silence surrounding northern recruitment service (5,4)

indicators.note: to surround something is to stand all round it, so GAG goes round N

annotation.surface: A story about a media blackout imposed around the north.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a news gag order; the answer is the gang that once seized men for the navy, a 'recruitment service' only in the grimmest sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A wry description: the gangs forcibly enlisted sailors for the Royal Navy, recruitment by kidnap.

clue.text: American people originally support helping to catch one taking assets (13)

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only the first letter of people is used
to catch something is to hold it, so RATION holds I inside

blocks.note: a helping of food is a ration; it opens after its R

annotation.surface: A sentence about Americans supporting the capture of an asset-stripper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'helping to catch one' looks like assistance to the police; 'helping' is a portion of food, and 'one' is the Roman numeral.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names the act of seizing property or funds for oneself.

clue.text: Mormon finally taken beneath Salt Lake (4)

indicators.note: what comes finally comes at the end, so only the last letter of Mormon is used
in a down answer, what is beneath comes lower, so N goes below TAR

blocks.note: an old salt and a tar are both sailors

annotation.surface: A Mormon heads to Salt Lake City, the church's home in Utah.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salt Lake' is a single place in the surface, but the words part company: Salt is a sailor and Lake alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: in the north of England a small mountain lake goes by this name.

clue.text: Plays lacking the ne plus ultra, broadcast rarities in the end (7-7)

indicators.note: a word lacking something goes without it, so RARITIES loses IT
seed that is broadcast is scattered, so the remaining letters are strewn into a new order
one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the rearranged letters go inside CURTAINS

blocks.note: 'it's curtains' means it's the end; it opens to take the rest before its S
IT is the ultimate, the very thing, as in 'this is it'
loses I and T, leaving RARIES to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A theatre programme boasts of rarities broadcast at last, plays lacking only the very best.
annotation.walkthrough: Ne plus ultra is Latin for 'nothing further', the highest point, and IT means the same thing in English. Take IT from RARITIES, jumble what is left, and drop it into CURTAINS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: these are the short pieces staged before the main play of an evening.

clue.text: Having no time, transported for charge (3)

indicators.note: a word having no T has had its T taken away, so RAPT drops it

annotation.surface: A convict is transported without a moment's notice to answer a charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'transported' suggests the old penal transportation beside 'charge', but it means enraptured.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense, as in 'take the rap' or 'a murder rap': the accusation a criminal faces.

clue.text: This for cleaner habits in such brothels possibly? (7,5)

indicators.note: what is possibly so might be otherwise, so SUCH BROTHELS is one possible order of the letters, not the answer's

annotation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that brothels could use something to smarten up their habits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Habits' pulls toward vice beside 'brothels'; here habits are clothes, as a monk's habit, and cleaner ones need brushing.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on habits as garments: the tool that brushes the dust off clothing makes them cleaner.

clue.text: Heard Hungarian composer’s record (4)

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by ear, so the answer is the sound of the composer's name

annotation.surface: Someone listens to a recording by Liszt.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive, a composer's record; for the wordplay it is simply 'is', joining sound to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a written catalogue of items is a record of them, and to enter them is to record them.

clue.text: Managed singular scheme teetotaller adopts in tricky operation (10)

indicators.note: to adopt is to take someone into your family, so TT takes RAN S PLAN inside

blocks.note: TT = teetotal; it opens to hold the rest

annotation.surface: A teetotaller manages a tricky scheme on their own.
annotation.walkthrough: TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal, and it splits to wrap everything else.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: moving an organ from one body to another is surgery at its most delicate.

clue.text: Something like onion tea filling energy gap (8)

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so CHA goes inside SLOT

blocks.note: a slot is a narrow gap; it opens after its S
cha (char) is British slang for tea

annotation.surface: A cook brews an onion-flavoured tea to fill an energy gap.
annotation.walkthrough: CHA for tea is worth learning; it is the common crossword stand-in. The E comes first, then SLOT holding CHA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by likeness: this old spelling of shallot names a small bulb of the onion family.

clue.text: Oxford official on speed one to gather papers? (7,4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing on another sits above it, so BULLDOG comes before CLIP

blocks.note: at Oxford and Cambridge a bulldog is a proctor's attendant
going at a clip = going at speed

annotation.surface: An Oxford university official on amphetamines rushing round to collect documents.
annotation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug; it is a rate, CLIP. The question mark marks the definition as playful, since the clip gathers papers rather than any person.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: the spring clip holds a sheaf of papers together, gathering them the way an official might.

clue.text: United defender moving — not supply enough? (9)

indicators.note: letters that are moving are shifted from their places, so DEFENDER is rearranged

blocks.note: U = United, as in football team names

annotation.surface: A football pundit wonders whether a United defender changing clubs means the team is short of cover.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface (United, defender, moving) hides a dieting word; the question mark covers a definition that is a verb phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by paraphrase: the verb is about food specifically, giving too little of it.

clue.text: Woodland creature rustic situated at the back (4)

blocks.note: an old word for a farm labourer, a third meaning
as with an animal's back legs

annotation.surface: A country dweller spots a deer lurking at the back of the wood.
annotation.walkthrough: Three meanings in a row: the deer, the farmhand and the adjective. 'Rustic' reads as describing the creature but is a definition of its own.
annotation.definitionFit: One word with three senses: the female deer, the old farmhand, and the adjective for the rear.

clue.text: Leader in religious house very worthy (8)

blocks.note: the title of the head of a convent or monastery, as in Mother ___

annotation.surface: Praise for the head of a monastery as a thoroughly admirable person.
annotation.walkthrough: The two meanings run together as one compliment to an abbot; split after 'house'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a title for the head of a religious community, and an adjective for high merit.

clue.text: Imperial theatre in Italian city going west (7)

definitions.note: Imperial is used here as a noun, one of imperial rank

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so REP goes inside ROME
on a map west is to the left, so in an across answer the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the Italian capital; it opens after RO

annotation.surface: A repertory company in Rome heads westward on tour.
annotation.walkthrough: Put REP into ROME to get ROREPME, then read it right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective stands as a noun for the person at the top of imperial rank.

clue.text: Militaristic state’s country chasing power (7)

indicators.note: a chaser runs behind what it chases, so RUSSIA comes after P

annotation.surface: A history lesson on a warlike state whose land grab followed its hunger for power.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive; it is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical description: the kingdom at the core of German unification was famous for its army.

clue.text: Youth working next to church green (7)

indicators.note: what is next to something sits beside it, so LAD ON follows CE

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A young man is at work beside the church on the village green.
annotation.walkthrough: 'church green' reads as one place; the definition is 'green' alone, and CE is the Church of England.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific shade for a general colour: the pale grey-green of a classic Chinese glaze.

clue.text: Exhausted drunk swallowing hard (4)

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so SOT takes H in

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard; it opens after its S

annotation.surface: An exhausted drunk downs another stiff one.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drinker knocking back hard liquor; 'hard' is only the pencil grading H.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense, as in 'my nerves are shot': worn out, used up.

clue.text: Tactless Parisian left (6)

blocks.note: the French word for the left-hand side

annotation.surface: A clumsy Parisian walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as a verb, someone departing; it is the direction, and the Parisian makes it French.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing: English took the French for left-handed and gave it the sense of social clumsiness.

clue.text: Circular letter, in Occitan, translated in joint effort (8)

indicators.note: the letter placed in the word joins its letters
a translated text is turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A circular letter written in Occitan is translated by a team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circular letter' looks like a mailshot; it is O, the letter shaped like a circle. Occitan is the Romance language of southern France.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal word built from co- and action: acting together, which a joint effort is.

clue.text: Man’s man? (8)

blocks.note: the surface reads a man's possessive; the setter means the Isle of Man
so the man belonging to it is a native of that island

annotation.surface: A phrase for a very masculine fellow's fellow.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital M is the trick: Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, and a native of it is an islander.
annotation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on an island, so a general word for any island-dweller fits him.

clue.text: Bitter spies heading north to check police department (6)

indicators.note: on a map north is up, so in a down answer the letters climb and read backwards
to check something is to hold it back, so the spies hold the department inside

blocks.note: the CIA, the US spy agency; it opens after its A
CID = Criminal Investigation Department, the British detective branch

annotation.surface: Resentful spies head north to investigate the police.
annotation.walkthrough: 'check' reads as investigate, spies checking up on police; it means restrain, which is why it signals a container.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a sharp, sour remark or temper is called acidic, as a bitter one is.

clue.text: An Italian getting on with war god unexpectedly (8)

blocks.note: una is Italian for a or an
Ares, the Greek god of war

annotation.surface: An Italian surprisingly finds himself on good terms with Mars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An Italian' looks like a man from Italy; it is the word 'an' translated into Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be caught or taken this way is to be surprised, so it stands for unexpectedly.

clue.text: Evaluates idiots on the distaff side? (8)

blocks.note: an invented word for female fools, built like lionesses

annotation.surface: Someone judges fools on the women's side of the family.
annotation.walkthrough: The distaff side is the female line. Add the feminine -ESS to ASS and pluralise, and the silly coinage spells the real verb.
annotation.definitionFit: One real sense, judging value, and one joke coinage, female asses; the question mark owns up to the second.

clue.text: Dissolute earl and San Franciscan go into party (7,8,8)

indicators.note: dissolute literally means loosened, dissolved, so the letters come apart and recombine

annotation.surface: A debauched aristocrat and a Californian join a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'and' is the one word left out of the fodder, joining the two sets of letters. 'go into' reads as joining the party but is fodder too.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this is a political party, South Africa's governing one since 1994.

clue.text: Relative’s very modest salary? (7)

blocks.note: a grand is £1,000, a very modest sum for a year's work
p.a. = per annum, the way salaries are quoted

annotation.surface: A complaint that a relative earns almost nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds; a thousand a year is 'very modest', which is the joke behind the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a grandfather is one kind of relative.

clue.text: Puzzling item bank opens (8)

indicators.note: to open something is to split it apart, so ROW goes into the gap in THING

blocks.note: an item is a thing; it opens after TH
a bank of seats or keys is a row

annotation.surface: A strange item turns up when the bank opens its doors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bank opens' looks like opening hours; 'opens' means ROW prises THING apart.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: a question that throws you knocks you off balance, puzzling you.

clue.text: Get down initially from rocky shelf (6)

indicators.note: what happens initially happens at the start, so only the first letter of from is used

blocks.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf of rock

annotation.surface: A climber is told to come down from a rocky ledge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get down' reads as an order to descend; the down is a young bird's soft feathers.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on down as feathers: a nestling that grows its feathers is getting its down.

clue.text: Corrupt Hughes to get VIP pass (4,2,3,5)

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoilt from its proper form, so the letters are twisted into a new order

annotation.surface: A bent official named Hughes wangles a VIP pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'VIP pass' reads as one thing, a backstage ticket; 'pass' alone is the definition, as in pass away.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for dying, matching pass in its sense of pass away.

clue.text: Knight cutting costs to swindle kind regal figures (7,7)

indicators.note: a knife cutting something goes into it, so N goes into PRICES

blocks.note: costs are prices; they open after PRI

annotation.walkthrough: N is the chess knight, since K is taken by the king. 'kind regal figures' reads as generous royals; 'kind' is SORT.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: husbands of reigning queens are royal personages.

clue.text: Arrested hen, minus tail, over commotion (6,2)

indicators.note: minus means take away, so PULLET loses its tail, its last letter

blocks.note: a pullet is a young hen; its tail, T, goes

annotation.walkthrough: 'hen' is too short a word to curtail usefully; the setter wants PULLET, a young hen, cut to PULLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Police slang: a suspect taken to the station has been brought in, arrested.

clue.text: Meet face to face under main promenade (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under sits lower, so FRONT comes after SEA

blocks.note: the main is the open sea
to front up is to face someone

annotation.surface: Two people arrange to meet in person on the prom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'main' is the poetic word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Deprive of land etc: cutting out sons here and there settles things (8)

indicators.note: to cut something out is to remove it, so letters come away

annotation.walkthrough: DISPOSSESS has four S's after the first; knock out two of them, leaving DISPOSES.

clue.text: Welfare professionals look worried with air crew carried in ship (6,7)

clue.text: Work with part containing single name for rival (8)

clue.text: With model after love at first sight (8)

annotation.walkthrough: 'love at first sight' is one idiom in the surface; split it, and 'sight' alone is the definition while 'love at first' gives L.

clue.text: On a roll, partner seen with revolutionary Irish breadhead? (11)

clue.text: Secret plan with fees involved deception (5,9)

clue.text: Obvious sport bags in supermarket (5,2,3)

clue.text: College staff conserving waste material (6)

clue.text: Duke leaving Saxon monarch’s company outside (8)

clue.text: Activity to dismiss as perplexing? (8)

clue.text: Fish people periodically want (7)

clue.text: Tramp going through waste pipe (4)

clue.text: Active period with Mike absent — say nothing (2,3,2)

clue.text: Yes, at rehab Clara regularly fails — this? (12)

definitions.text: Yes, at rehab Clara regularly fails — this?

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of Clara is taken
something that fails breaks down, so the letters break up and are rearranged

annotation.surface: Clara, in rehab, keeps failing the test.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone in rehab for drink who fails regularly would fail a breathalyser.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the roadside alcohol test a relapsing drinker keeps failing.

clue.text: Hampstead Heath cleaner, tense, osteopath treated (10)

indicators.note: a patient who is treated is worked on and changed, so the letters are reworked into a new order

annotation.surface: A tense patient is seen by an osteopath and a cleaner on Hampstead Heath.
annotation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is Cockney rhyming slang for teeth (it is a park in north London), so the cleaner is for teeth.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: Hampstead Heath means teeth, and this is what cleans them.
